doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

chapter: Social life of old New Orleans
title: Safety, summer nights and entertainment in old New Orleans
summary: Jim and others recall doors left open, cabarets and dance halls everywhere, and worry about youngsters today.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: They had so much entertainment here in this town here in the city here that people didn't have to wonder where to go because the age and every way you turn around is somewhere you can go and have a good time. Yeah, cabarets, dance halls. And you could walk the street with $5,000 in your pocket. No, no. You want to catch you?
Put a pad in what you do.
Go to sleep. Go to sleep.
Go to sleep. Go to sleep. Ain't no water coming in there. We had no air conditioning. Don't you try it now.

And you had to have money to have like these ceiling fans like some of the old-time houses. Oh, no, no, no. But I lived on Two Road Street. We had to get mosquito balls and didn't lock the front door, didn't lock the back door. Sometime this didn't have no screams, nothing like this. Just leave the door alone. Let the kitchen door wide open. Sleep right on the pallet. Nobody gon' bother. Women, men. I walked the street many hours at night when I was a young man. And go to and fro from the economy hall. I didn't have no money to get no street calls. Used to run on the hours. So there ain't no calls. I come down from the economy hall. Come to Two Road Street. Nobody gon' bother. People don't study much.

The youngsters more better. That's it. You gotta watch the youngsters. They're the ones that do all the dentments and do a lot of wrong things. The person has good kids. Some of them want to see the list to come back. They ain't from the trouble. The only one went to one time they got no business.
